deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. The folio is the verso of the printed bookseller's notification form of Carl Röttger, Kaiserlicher Hofbuchhändler, St. Petersburg (Platzfirma H. Schmitzdorff). What appears is not independent writing. It is the mirror-image show-through (or offset) of the recto, which is the previous page in the sequence. Every element is laterally reversed: the printed letterhead 'Carl Röttger / Kaiserlicher Hofbuchhändler / Platzfirma: H. Schmitzdorff', the double-eagle emblem, 'St. Petersburg', 'den', 'zur Nachricht', the zig-zag border, and the handwriting. Read in reverse, the text matches the recto exactly. Röttger's message: 'Herrn G. C. E. Meyer sen. in Braunschweig zur Nachricht, daß "Zolotareff, théorie des nombres entiers etc." nicht zu beschaffen, da das Werk hier gänzlich vergriffen ist. — Hochachtungsvoll [signature]', dated 'den 10/6 76'. Below it, in fainter ink, is the Braunschweig bookseller Meyer's annotation to Dedekind: 'Ich werde versuchen, ob ein Exemplar antiquarisch aufzutreiben. Hochachtend G C E Meyer'. Historical context: in June 1876 Dedekind was trying to obtain, through his Braunschweig bookseller, E. I. Zolotarev's 'Théorie des nombres entiers complexes' (Russian original, St. Petersburg 1874). Zolotarev's alternative approach to ideal theory was only later published in French (J. Math. Pures Appl. 1880). The next page is Meyer's letter of 20/6 76 reporting that he re-ordered the work from the publisher. This is bibliographic and correspondence material only; nothing can be reconstructed mathematically.
errors: The machine transcription treats the page as an independent text. In fact it is the mirror-image bleed-through of the recto, so its readings ('J. C. Meyer', 'Filiale', 'Soch.', 'noch') are garbled versions of the recto text.

results.what: Documentary evidence that Dedekind sought Zolotarev's 'Théorie des nombres entiers complexes' (1874) in June 1876 via the bookseller G. C. E. Meyer, and that the work was out of print in St. Petersburg
results.modern_name: Biographical/bibliographic evidence (Dedekind's awareness of Zolotarev's ideal theory)

deep.surprise_reason: No mathematical content; the page is only show-through of a bookseller's notice. The minor historical detail that Dedekind tried to obtain Zolotarev's 1874 thesis in 1876 is mildly interesting for the history of ideal theory, but unremarkable.
